reviews.reason: The complete judgment gives the child-household parent in Poland priority through the EU whole-family residence fiction and EStG 64(2) sentence 1. It does not fabricate a common household for separated parents. The absence of a foreign-parent application does not transfer priority to the German applicant. Paragraph 21 conditions that result on the underlying entitlement requirements being met in the German claimant. The other national requirements remain necessary; the case does not create a universal foreign-parent entitlement. This instrument remains bearing and unencoded; it cannot be classified around as procedure or as a restatement. Exact BStBl II issue membership is not verified by this review.

The complete judgment applies the whole-family fiction to the divorced parent with the child in Poland. Paragraphs 23–25 use Article 1(i)(1)(i), not the fallback in Article 1(i)(2), to identify participants by national entitlement, including divorced parents. Article 60 is reached through Article 67 whether or not an Article 68 benefit conflict exists. Paragraphs 27–30 preserve the foreign-parent requirements and actual household facts; the other parent's application can be considered for the priority parent without transferring entitlement. Historic Polish and German payment figures are case facts, not current rate parameters. This instrument remains bearing and unencoded; it cannot be classified around as procedure or as a restatement. Exact BStBl II issue membership is not verified by this review.

The complete judgment remands because the Belgian-resident mother's remaining national entitlement requirements were not established. Article 60 fictions domestic residence, but does not remove EStG 62(2) conditions for a parent not entitled to free movement. The recognized refugee father falls within Article 2(1) through Article 1(g); this is not a rule that every third-country national automatically qualifies. Paragraphs 21–23 preserve the actual separate-household facts and the irrelevance of the other parent's missing German application to recipient priority. No unconditional award to the mother or current rate follows from this remand. This instrument remains bearing and unencoded; it cannot be classified around as procedure or as a restatement. Exact BStBl II issue membership is not verified by this review.

The complete judgment remands for actual household and other entitlement findings. Paragraph 24 requires consideration of a real common household in Germany and/or Hungary: EStG 64(2) sentences 2–4 may then govern recipient determination. The residence fiction alone neither establishes nor disproves that household. Paragraph 26 makes maintenance-rent priority under EStG 64(3) inapplicable while the child belongs to an entitled person's household. Paragraphs 20–23 preserve application and remaining-national-condition limits. Paragraph 25 concerns the temporal scope of the contested decision, not a new monthly entitlement test. This instrument remains bearing and unencoded; it cannot be classified around as procedure or as a restatement. Exact BStBl II issue membership is not verified by this review.

The complete judgment applies whole-family residence fiction and household priority despite a concurrent Bulgarian family benefit. State-level Article 68 coordination does not select the German-resident parent as the personal recipient. Paragraphs 20–24 include separated parents among participants, preserve other national conditions and do not turn separated households into a common household. Paragraphs 25–26 require consideration of the German applicant's application for the priority mother, without transferring priority because she did not apply. Historical foreign payments and differential amounts are case facts, not current rates. This instrument remains bearing and unencoded; it cannot be classified around as procedure or as a restatement. Exact BStBl II issue membership is not verified by this review.
